title: France Faces Twin Pressures of Fiscal Strain and Rising Unemployment Ahead of… · 26 Aug
keywords: France, budget deficit, unemployment, fiscal policy, eurozone, European Commission, INSEE, inflation, labor market, French politics, 2027 election, public spending, austerity, borrowing costs, EU fiscal rules
notes: France is grappling simultaneously with a widening budget deficit and a weakening labor market, combining to create a compound economic challenge for the government of Prime Minister Michel Barnier. With unemployment reaching 8.3 percent in the second quarter of 2026 and the deficit forecast to remain above five percent of GDP, Paris faces mounting pressure from both Brussels and its own voters. The twin crises are reshaping France's political landscape ahead of the 2027 presidential election and raising broader questions about eurozone stability.
